newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks dip as foreign funds stay away.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks dip as foreign funds stay away.

text.p: Colombian stocks were dragged down by bluechips Thursday as foreign funds stayed away amid a lack of news on second quarter results.
Bogota's IBB index fell 0.39 percent to 1,201.43 amid a 5.8 billion volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.03 percent to 18,301.39 amid a 2.5 billion peso volume.
"Trading was mediocre because foreign funds stayed away because there is still no information about second quarter results," one Bogota dealer said.
"There's been some partial results but the leading companies have still not published details," he added.
The Securities Superintendency was due to begin publishing second quarter results on July 22 but has not yet begun to do so.
One of the day's biggest decliners was brewing giant Bavaria down 1.02 percent to 8,215 in Bogota and down 0.05 percent to 8,295.3 in Medellin.
Banco Ganadero, Colombia's largest bank in terms of assets, dipped 0.73 percent to 407 in Bogota and 0.85 percent to the same price in Medellin.
Cement company Cemento Argos, one of the flagships of the giant Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, lost 0.74 percent dipping to 8,635 in Bogota.
